name: PropertyRow
summary: One row of a design tool's inspector: compact fields in a two-column grid with an action column at the end, as Figma's properties panel lays out X | Y, W | H and rotation | radius. Rows stack inside a PropertySection. Use small (xs) fields with inline glyphs or icons and hidden labels; the section's heading names the group. Not for a form's fields (use a Stack of fields with visible labels) or for facts (DescriptionList).
a11y: Adds no role: each field keeps its own accessible name (with `hideLabel`, the visible glyph or icon is a cue, the name is still read). The action is a Button with its own name.

props.name: children
props.description: The row's fields, in reading order: one, or a pair that sits side by side (X and Y, W and H, rotation and radius).

props.name: columns
props.description: `2` (default) puts the fields in two equal columns, wrapping a third onto the next line; `1` gives one field the whole row (a colour, a Select); `3` fits three short ones (an export's scale, suffix and format).

props.name: lead
props.description: With two fields, the first takes two thirds of the row: a colour (swatch and hex) beside its opacity, as Figma draws a fill.

props.name: action
props.description: Compact controls at the row's end that act on the row: remove it, show or hide it (an xs Switch). The column is held at one button's width on every row, so the fields line up whether a row has one or not; a second control widens only its own row.
